articles.title: Fast track to the slopes: 12 European ski resorts by rail – in less time than you may think
articles.description: For skiers looking to reduce their carbon footprint, rail travel from the UK to the Alps has never been quicker or easier. Here’s how to get there Speeding effortlessly towards the slopes by train, you might wonder why you ever flew to a ski resort. On paper, it seems a short hop by plane; in reality, airport queues, cramped flights and long transfers can mean the journey eats up a whole day. Measured door-to-door, daytime rail travel from London can be as fast as flying, while taking a sleeper train gets you extra time on the slopes. And with Alpine glaciers suffering significant loss of snow cover as global temperatures rise, rail travel constitutes the biggest emissions saving a skier can make. Continue reading...

articles.title: Cebu City clarifies: No ASF outbreak in Barangay Sapangdaku
articles.description: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The Cebu City Department of Veterinary Medicine and Fisheries (DVMF) clarified that there are no confirmed African swine fever (ASF)-positive cases in Barangay Sapangdaku, following reports of hog deaths and the establishment of a checkpoint to prevent the disease from spreading to other communities. The clarification came after the city intensified surveillance in the mountain barangay, where reports had circulated about the alleged presence of ASF. The DVMF said the checkpoint and other monitoring measures were preventive actions and did not mean an outbreak had been confirmed in Sapangdaku. articles.title: From Alaskan bears to baby bats, these lives cams are a treat
articles.description: Ever wanted to watch bears catch salmon in Alaska or elephants gather around a watering hole in Africa? You might not get the chance to see these events in person, but thanks to a cool website called Explore.org Live Cams, you can watch them from your computer. The free website features more than 200 live cameras set up in wildlife locations around the world. You can watch brown bears fishing at Brooks Falls in Alaska, check out the infamous Trempealeau Eagles in their nest, or get spooked by the eyeshine of Nile crocodiles on the Mara Fig Tree crossing night cam. The site also has live feeds of rescue kittens, puppies, and other animals living in shelters and care centers. I’m a big fan of the Mixed Species Flying Fox cam, which is set up at the Lubee Bat Conservancy in Gainesville. There’s just something about watching furry bats munching on fruit all day that warms the heart. Many of the cameras also include interesting facts about the animals, local weather information, and comment sections where you can chat with other people watching. There’s even a collection of snapshots so you can see what you might’ve missed. There’s no guarantee anything exciting will happen and you might spend half an hour staring at an empty riverbank. But that makes it all the more exciting when you do witness something. Just like the wildly popular Dutch Fish Doorbell, these live cams give you something relaxing to have on in the background while you work and help us connect with nature just a tad bit more, even in the confines of our cubicles. For more fun and helpful tips, tricks, website and app recommendations, be sure to subscribe to our PCWorld Try This newsletter.
